rationale: Concept and execution collapse cleanly: four live counts of the same string (graphemes, code points, UTF-16 units, UTF-8 bytes) are the argument, with the 'remaining' meter deliberately wired to String.length so it reddens faster than the eye justifies — the disagreement is the mechanism, not a decoration of it. The readymade move (the platform character counter as Duchampian infra-mince relocated) is fresh and earns its place next to Bochner's measurement tradition. Material is well-distinguished from COPY / COPY (which hides a byte-level difference behind identical rendering) and from La Disparition (which removes); here nothing is hidden, the string is fully visible, and the fracture lives in the counting itself.
reservations: The underlying technical fact (emoji span multiple UTF-16 units) is well-known in web development circles, so a chunk of the 'discovery' is pre-loaded for the literate viewer; the work leans on infra-mince to elevate what is otherwise a known curiosity. Narrative connection to the catalogue is more thematic than responsive to a specific prior work — it answers the tradition broadly rather than a single predecessor.
